extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants and patent practitioners seeking to participate in the USPTO–DKPTO Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) pilot program
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for requesting accelerated examination under the USPTO–DKPTO Patent Prosecution Highway pilot program, including eligibility, required documentation, filing method, and special examination rules. Intended to guide preparation and filing of a PPH request/petition in the U.S. application when DKPTO is the Office of First Filing (OFF) or vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application type and priority requirements (eligibility 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. application must be one of the specified types that validly claim priority/benefit to a DKPTO-filed application (Paris Convention, national stage under the PCT, or a bypass application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120), or in certain cases a PCT application with no priority claims as described in subparts (a)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes detailed subrequirements: (1)(a)(i) Paris route validly claiming priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a) and 37 CFR 1.55 to one or more DKPTO applications; (1)(a)(ii) Paris route claiming priority to a PCT that contains no priority claims; (1)(b) national stage (35 U.S.C. 371) where the PCT validly claims priority under 35 U.S.C. 365(b) to a DKPTO application or contains no priority claim; (1)(c) bypass (35 U.S.C. 111(a)) claiming benefit under 120 to a PCT that meets similar priority/no-priority conditions. The Annex contains multiple example routes (Paris, PCT, divisional, domestic priority) demonstrating acceptable priority/claim chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain application types are excluded from participation in the PPH pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications, plant and design applications, reissue applications, reexamination proceedings, and applications subject to a secrecy order are not eligible for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: DKPTO must have at least one allowable/patentable claim (eligibility 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DKPTO application(s) relied upon must have at least one claim determined by DKPTO to be allowable/patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must submit a copy of the allowable/patentable claims and an English translation with a statement that the translation is accurate if claims are not in English. If the DKPTO office action does not explicitly state a claim is allowable/patentable, the applicant must include a statement in the PPH request (or transmittal letter) that no rejection was made regarding that claim and thus it is deemed allowable/patentable by DKPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims correspondence requirement (eligibility 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims in the U.S. application for which PPH participation is requested must sufficiently correspond to the allowable/patentable claims in the DKPTO application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient correspondence is determined by whether, accounting for translation and claim format differences, claims are of the same or similar scope. Applicant must submit an English claims correspondence table indicating how each U.S. claim corresponds to the DKPTO allowable/patentable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination must not have begun (eligibility 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. application must not have been taken up for examination at the time the PPH participation request is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examination has already begun, the application is not eligible to be advanced under the PPH pilot program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for participation and petition to make special; fee (eligibility 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must file a request for participation in the PPH pilot program and a petition to make the U.S. application special under the PPH pilot program, and pay the required petition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sample request/petition form (PTO/SB/20DK) is provided by the USPTO and applicants are encouraged to use it. A petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) for the petition to make special under 37 CFR 1.102(d) is required. The petition to make special under the PPH pilot program follows procedures different from MPEP 708.02(a) accelerated examination petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of DKPTO office actions and translations (eligibility 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit copies of all DKPTO office actions that are relevant to patentability from each DKPTO application containing the allowable/patentable claims, with English translations and a statement of accuracy if not in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must also submit copies of any DKPTO office actions issued after grant of the PPH request in the USPTO (e.g., where DKPTO reversed prior allowability). If the U.S. application has not been published and Public PAIR cannot be used, applicant must provide necessary documents to DKPTO or request DKPTO obtain them from USPTO Public PAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS listing and copies of documents cited by DKPTO examiner (eligibility 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must file an information disclosure statement (IDS) listing the documents cited by the DKPTO examiner in the DKPTO office action, unless such an IDS has already been filed in the U.S. application, and must provide copies of those documents (with exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of all documents cited in the DKPTO office action must be submitted unless already filed in the U.S. application. Exception: do not submit copies of U.S. patents or U.S. patent application publications. Filing these items helps satisfy duties under MPEP § 2001.06(a), but does not eliminate duty of candor under 37 CFR 1.56 and 37 CFR 10.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit PPH request and document indexing (filing method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for participation in the PPH pilot program and all supporting documents must be submitted to the USPTO via EFS-Web and indexed with a specific document description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index the PPH request as: “Petition to make special under Patent Pros Hwy.” Preliminary amendments and IDSs submitted with the PPH documents must be separately indexed as a preliminary amendment and IDS, respectively. Information on EFS-Web is available at the USPTO EFS help pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to cure defects in PPH request; examiner action not suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PPH request does not meet requirements, applicant will be notified of defects and given one opportunity to perfect the request via a renewed request; examiner action is not suspended while the applicant perfects the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is picked up for examination after notice of defects, any renewed request will be dismissed. If the renewed request is perfected and examination has not begun, special status will be granted and the application advanced. If not perfected, the application will await regular turn. Thus applicants should perfect promptly; perfection after examination begins will be ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH status does not carry over to continuing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant of participation in the PPH pilot program and special status for a parent application does not automatically carry over to a continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each continuing application must separately satisfy all PPH conditions and submit its own request and supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special examination priority and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once PPH participation and special status are granted, the U.S. application will be taken up for examination ahead of other categories except certain high-priority categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications advanced under PPH are examined before other categories except those clearly in condition for allowance, those with set time limits (e.g., examiner’s answers), and those granted special status for “accelerated examination.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant claim amendments must correspond; non-responsive treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claims amended or added after grant of PPH participation must sufficiently correspond to one or more allowable/patentable claims in the DKPTO application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must submit an updated claims correspondence table with the amendment. If amended or newly added claims do not sufficiently correspond, the amendment will not be entered and will be treated as a non-responsive reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor and continuing disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in the PPH pilot program does not relieve applicants of obligations under 37 CFR 1.56 (duty to disclose material information) and 37 CFR 10.18 (duty of candor), and applicants remain responsible for submitting material information known to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By providing DKPTO office actions and the IDS listing documents cited by the DKPTO examiner (per requirements (6) and (7)), applicants are considered to have complied with duties to bring to USPTO material prior art cited in the corresponding foreign application(s) (see MPEP § 2001.06(a)). However, applicants must still disclose other material information known to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: DKPTO basis application may be different from U.S. priority application; relationship must be identified
rubrics_metrics.description: The DKPTO application that contains the allowable/patentable claims does not have to be the DKPTO application for which priority is claimed in the U.S. application (it may be a divisional or other derived application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the DKPTO application containing the allowable/patentable claims is not the same application for which priority is claimed in the U.S. application, the applicant must identify the relationship between the DKPTO application with allowable claims and the DKPTO priority application claimed in the U.S. (for example, identify that DKPTO application X is a divisional of DKPTO application Y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial period, evaluation, extension and termination conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPH pilot program commences November 3, 2008 for one year ending November 3, 2009, may be extended up to one additional year, and is subject to evaluation and possible early termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO and DKPTO will evaluate the pilot to determine if and how to fully implement the PPH after the trial. Either office may terminate early if participation volume becomes unmanageable or for other reasons; notice will be published if termination occurs before the scheduled end date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously-filed documents in the U.S. application need not be resubmitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the documents required by items (2), (6), and (7) have already been filed in the U.S. application prior to the PPH request, the applicant does not need to resubmit them with the PPH request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may simply refer to those documents and indicate in the PPH request when they were previously filed in the U.S. application. This can reduce duplication when using Public PAIR or previously submitted material.
